# Pikos

> Notes, tasks, and calendar in one on-device desktop app.

Pikos is a desktop productivity app for macOS and Linux that combines notes, tasks, and a calendar into a single interface. All data is stored on the user's device. No account required, no sign-up, no cloud dependency.

## Key Facts

- Category: Productivity / Notes / Task Management / Calendar
- Platform: macOS and Linux
- Pricing: Free desktop download (no limits, no trial). A Mac App Store version (with iCloud sync) and an iPhone app are planned, each a one-time purchase. No subscriptions. A $29 Backer pre-order is available at pikos.app/backer for early supporters; backers receive the paid App Store apps free when they ship.
- Data: Stored on device. Export anytime.
- Privacy: No telemetry, no tracking cookies, no personal data collection.
- Source: Source-available. Full code public on GitHub (not open-source licensed).
- Website: https://pikos.app
- Contact: hello@pikos.app

## What Pikos Does

- Rich text editor with slash commands, formatting toolbar, Markdown paste, and autosave
- Task management with priorities (Urgent/High/Medium/Low), statuses, tags, and folders
- Week calendar view with drag-to-schedule, timed and all-day events
- External calendar sync: read-only, opt-in, from iCloud, Google Calendar, or any CalDAV server. Synced events become pages you can take notes on. Nothing written in Pikos is sent back to the provider. Credentials are held in the operating system keychain
- Quick add with natural language parsing (extracts dates, priorities, tags, folders)
- Full-text search with BM25 ranking
- Recurring pages and recurring calendar events, sharing one recurrence engine
- Reminders and a notification history
- Three-panel layout: sidebar, page list, editor or calendar
- Complete keyboard navigation
- Light, dark, and system themes
- Data export (SQLite backup, CSV, Markdown, ICS)
- A command-line interface, `pikos`, that reads and writes the same workspace file
- An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, `pikos mcp`, over stdio, so an AI agent can search, read, create and update pages locally. It opens no network socket

## Network Behaviour

Pikos works offline. Notes, tasks and the calendar all function with no connection.

It makes network requests in exactly two cases, both visible to the user:

1. An update check against GitHub Releases at launch, which can be turned off in Settings.
2. External calendar sync, if and only if you connect a calendar account. It is off until you do, it only reads, and it talks to your calendar provider and nothing else.

There is no Pikos server. No account, no telemetry, no analytics inside the app.

## Who Pikos Is For

- People who want notes, tasks, and a calendar in one app instead of three
- Users who care about data ownership and on-device storage
- Anyone who wants a productivity app with no account, no subscription, and no cloud dependency
- Obsidian users who wish they had built-in tasks and a calendar
- TickTick or Todoist users who want a real note editor alongside their tasks
- Privacy-conscious users who don't want their data on someone else's server
- People who want an AI agent to work with their notes and tasks locally, without handing them to a cloud service

## Competitors and Alternatives

Pikos competes with Notion, NotePlan, Obsidian, Logseq, TickTick, Things, and Todoist, and with the combination of Apple Notes, Reminders and Calendar.

| Feature             | Pikos | NotePlan | Notion | Obsidian | Logseq | TickTick | Things | Todoist |
|---------------------|-------|----------|--------|----------|--------|----------|--------|---------|
| Rich Notes          | Yes   | Yes      | Yes    | Yes      | Yes    | No       | No     | No      |
| Task Management     | Yes   | Yes      | Yes    | No       | Yes    | Yes      | Yes    | Yes     |
| Built-in Calendar   | Yes   | Yes      | Yes    | No       | No     | Yes      | No     | No      |
| On-device storage   | Yes   | Yes      | No     | Yes      | Yes    | No       | Yes    | No      |
| No Account Required | Yes   | No       | No     | Yes      | Yes    | No       | Yes    | No      |
| Free                | Yes   | No       | Yes    | Yes      | Yes    | No       | No     | No      |
| Source Available    | Yes   | No       | No     | No       | Yes    | No       | No     | No      |

Logseq is the closest on data ownership: local-first, no account, and open source, but it has no calendar. Notion is the closest on breadth: it does notes, tasks and a calendar too, but keeps your work on its servers and requires an account.

Pikos differentiates by being the only one of these that combines notes, tasks, and a calendar while staying on-device, free, source-available, and usable with no account.

Checked September 2026.
